newsitem.title: SURINAM: Ex-military gov't leader named Surinam president.
newsitem.headline: Ex-military gov't leader named Surinam president.

text.p: Surinam's top regional and national politicians on Thursday chose a leading member of the former military government to run the country in the closest presidential vote since independence from the Netherlands.
Jules Wijdenbosch, 55, who is backed by former military strongman Desi Bouterse, defeated current President Ronald Venetiaan by 438 votes to 407, National Assembly Speaker Jaggernath Lachmon said.
"With this result Jules Wijdenbosch is the new president of the country," Lachmon said after the votes had been counted.
Wijdenbosch's supporters in the national sports centre where the vote took place burst into applause and sang the national anthem after learning the result.

The tense vote ended months of political uncertainty following unclear general election results in May. Neither Venetiaan's New Front coalition nor Wijdenbosch's National Democratic Party (NDP) secured the two-thirds majority necessary to form a government in the May elections.
This outcome forced Thursday's vote of the United Peoples Assembly (VVV) which includes over 800 national, regional and district politicians.
